_meta.indication: KERYDIN (tavaborole) topical solution, 5% is an oxaborole antifungal indicated for the treatment of onychomycosis of the toenails due to Trichophyton rubrum or Trichophyton mentagrophytes.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults age 18 and older with a clinical diagnosis of onychomycosis, 20-60% involvement of target toenail, positive KOH, and positive culture.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of the target toenail plus negative KOH and negative culture)
pivotal_trials.result: Complete cure 6.5% (26/399) tavaborole vs 0.5% (1/194) vehicle; p=0.001

pivotal_trials.population: Adults age 18 and older with a clinical diagnosis of onychomycosis, 20-60% involvement of target toenail, positive KOH, and positive culture.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of the target toenail plus negative KOH and negative culture)
pivotal_trials.result: Complete cure 9.1% (36/396) tavaborole vs 1.5% (3/205) vehicle; p<0.001

key_safety: Common adverse reactions (≥1%) were application site exfoliation (2.7% vs 0.3% vehicle), ingrown toenail (2.5% vs 0.3%), application site erythema (1.6% vs 0%), and application site dermatitis (1.3% vs 0%). Systemic exposure was low with no systemic toxicities identified.
target_moa: Tavaborole inhibits fungal protein synthesis by inhibiting an aminoacyl-transfer RNA (tRNA) synthetase (AARS).

rems.type: Risk mitigation measures beyond professional labeling are not warranted for Kerydin.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; tavaborole presented no novel or complex regulatory issues requiring advisory committee input.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients ages 6 to 16 years and 11 months (fulfilled pediatric study requirement)

citations.quote: We note that you have fulfilled the pediatric study requirement for ages 6 to 16 years and 11 months for this application.

summary.text: Kerydin (tavaborole) was a 505(b)(1) new drug application for a new molecular entity (NME) submitted by Anacor Pharmaceuticals, approved full approval for toenail onychomycosis based on two vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials, with a deferred pediatric (PREA) postmarketing requirement; no advisory committee was needed.

citations.quote: This is a 505 (b)(1) new drug application for a new molecular entity (NME), tavaborole, submitted by Anacor Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
Your deferred pediatric study required by section 505B(a) of the FDCA is a required postmarketing study.
Tavaborole, a new oxaborole antifungal, though an NME, presented no novel or complex regulatory issues that required the input of an advisory committee.

requirement.text: PMR 2154-1: Pharmacokinetic/safety study of tavaborole topical solution, 5% in 40 pediatric subjects age 12 to 17 years and 11 months with onychomycosis of the toenails, with PK assessments in at least 16 evaluable subjects under maximal use conditions.

citations.quote: PMR 2154-1 Pharmacokinetic/safety study of tavaborole topical solution, 5% in 40 pediatric subjects age 12 to 17 years and 11 months with onychomycosis of the toenails.
Pharmacokinetic assessments will be done in at least 16 evaluable subjects under maximal use conditions.
